criteria.label: Value realised
criteria.definition: The customer describes a change in how their work goes since they started using it — time no longer spent, a step that no longer happens, a number that moved, a problem that stopped recurring. It does not have to be quantified. Praise for the product with no change described is not enough.

criteria.label: Adoption known
criteria.definition: The customer says who is using it and how much, including when the answer is that hardly anyone is. A number, a named team, or a plain statement that usage is narrow or has fallen all count.

criteria.label: Renewal risk named
criteria.definition: The customer says anything that makes renewing less certain. This is deliberately broad: narrow or falling usage, a competing priority that will take their attention, a budget or procurement review, a champion or sponsor moving on, an alternative they are considering, an unresolved complaint, or doubt about whether it is worth the price. A risk stated calmly is still a risk.

criteria.label: Decision process known
criteria.definition: The customer describes how the renewal actually gets decided — who signs it off, what review or procurement step it goes through, or when the decision happens. Any one of those counts.

criteria.label: Expansion interest
criteria.definition: The customer raises a team, a use case, an integration or a capability beyond what they have today, including as a condition rather than a request. Asked about and declined counts as observed, not confirmed.
